reason: Four bus/endpoint registration extensions preserve explicit serializer/deserializer selection, null validation, and the optional package boundary; no duplicate registration policy is introduced here.
The public advanced factory exposes one lazy, shared, thread-safe serializer/deserializer instance and the declared media type; configuration extensions are its application-facing entry point.
Internal typed delegate holder has one concrete-formatter responsibility and validates each constructor dependency; no public API leaks from it.
Internal weak-key and Lazy cache compiles an installed concrete formatter invoker once while avoiding a permanent strong type-key table; reflection and delegate creation occur on a cache miss.
Declared interface-to-concrete wire mapping preserves the known representation and rejects an incompatible runtime implementation before encoding.
Interface contracts use a generated declared implementation for reads and a compatible runtime concrete type for writes; the weak-key invoker cache owns dynamic access.

Initial object-valued inline cast defect was reproduced red and corrected in bac2c88f9 with a typed BytesInlineMessageData<T> object branch; final MessagePack 115/115 and UnitArchitecture 9,535/9,535 are green. Original source-admission hash is a pre-fix snapshot.

Internal envelope applies the shared serializer-independent metadata projection, retains explicit wire fields, and copies mutable payload bytes across forwarding snapshots; no duplicate clock or TTL rule remains.

Overlay preserves case-insensitive recursive object merge and array append, but deserializes the whole payload and builds several JSON/MessagePack trees before downstream send admission; establish a bounded depth and peak-memory proof on Embedded before A+ acceptance.

The send path applies body and envelope admission before provider I/O and owns returned bytes; its body-buffer to array to envelope-clone to envelope-buffer copies need aggregate peak-memory evidence under the Embedded profile.

The advanced serializer supports envelope, object, Base64, probe and copied-body extraction, but inbound body.ToArray and eagerly decoded Base64 require path-level evidence that admission precedes large materialization; no test or code change made here.
One internal resolver/options owner applies MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData on all module serialization and deserialization calls; bounded writers are supplied by the admitted transport-body path.

Internal serializer context exposes supported contract decoding, cancellation propagation, forwarding and dictionary projection; malformed contract payloads return false by the existing tested TryGetMessage contract.

One internal formatter owner maps ServiceBus special interfaces and MessageData<T>, defers unrelated concrete types, and caches constructed formatters with weak type keys; no application API is added.

Optional net10.0 package has matching project/package/root identity, centrally versioned MessagePack dependencies, direct references to both assemblies used by its source, a required signing import, and no custom target or script anti-pattern; RootNamespace and Nullable repeat effective defaults but cause no demonstrated failure.
